title: Let extensions contribute MCP servers — DESIGN ONLY, no build under M2
wave: 8 (Thiết kế hoãn: lưu trạng thái extension và MCP — WI-11, WI-12. S mỗi cái, không build)
one_line: Write a decision document that picks one of two architectures for letting a loaded extension hand an MCP server to the core manager — the recommended one registers a server descriptor that core's existing manager instantiates — and state the approval and trust rules out loud, because this item ships a decision and not a line of code.
user_visible_effect: none — internal. This work item writes one design document and changes no runtime behavior. Nothing in the tree ships under M2: the plan (§8.2) explicitly records that MCP contribution has no owner, no milestone, and no scheduled build.
written_to: docs/mcp-server-contribution-by-extensions.md (new, ADR-shaped), with a one-line pointer added to docs/extensions.md and docs/mcp-config.md. No source file changes.
effort: S to write (a decision document plus a pointer line, half a day), M to build — and the build is NOT scheduled under M2 by this item, it only becomes possible after WI-0 and WI-10 land.
risk: Writing the design as if the approval question were already settled. Contributing a server is a different kind of trust decision from contributing a tool — it carries a connection lifecycle, a credential path, and an outbound network destination — and it inherits WI-0's unanswered posture, which is not merely undecided but hardcoded permissive: isProjectTrusted() is `() => true` at BOTH runner.ts:1264 and session/agent-session.ts:7406. If the doc names a trust tier without answering that, the implementation will pick one silently and the shipped behavior will be whatever MCPManager happens to do.
depends_on: WI-0 — the extension trust model must be decided and written first. Verified as not merely open but stubbed: `isProjectTrusted(): boolean` is declared at extensions/types.ts:494 and :561 and implemented as `() => true` at extensions/runner.ts:1264 and session/agent-session.ts:7406. An extension-contributed MCP server inherits that check, and today it cannot fail.

WI-10 — must state, as an explicit YES/NO/DEFERRED, which of the five (or six) write surfaces is canonical for MCP contribution. This design doc is not allowed to quietly become that answer; if it does, WI-10 has been pre-empted.
blocks: Nothing inside M2. The build this design unblocks is unowned per §8.2 and must be given a name and a deadline before M2 closes — that assignment is a human decision this spec does not make.

plan_corrections.verdict: STALE AND MATERIALLY OVERSTATED — the premise is half wrong, and the wrong half changes which architecture is correct
plan_corrections.correction: The ExtensionAPI half is right: `ExtensionAPI` (extensions/types.ts:1256) declares no MCP-contribution method, and the only MCP members are inbound (types.ts:663, :665, :1340, :904-916). But an extension PACKAGE already contributes MCP servers today, declaratively. Three providers register the mcps capability: `registerProvider<MCPServer>(mcpCapability.id, …)` at discovery/omp-plugins.ts:423, discovery/agent-plugins.ts:335, and discovery/claude-plugins.ts:737 — 12 providers register it in total. omp-plugins reads `.mcp.json` / `mcp.json` from the package root (`MCP_FILENAMES` at omp-plugins.ts:275, `loadMCPServers` at :293-370, registered at :423), and docs/mcp-config.md:40 and :489-491 already document extension packages as an MCP source ranked #2 in discovery precedence. The real gap is therefore narrower and must be stated as: a LOADED, LIVE extension module cannot contribute a server IMPERATIVELY at runtime. That distinction is load-bearing — Option B below is not merely disfavored, it is a regression against a path that already ships.

plan_corrections.claim: Plan §WI-12 'Chỗ dễ sai' and 'Test cần viết': the approval-parity proposition ('tools of an extension-registered MCP server appear through the normal MCP tool path, with the same approval gating as any other tool') is the thing that distinguishes the recommended design from the config-write option.
plan_corrections.verdict: UNDERSPECIFIED — the proposition cannot be checked as written, because the current tiers are not what the plan assumes
plan_corrections.correction: Write it with the actual numbers, and note that today's state is itself an artifact. `MCPTool.approval` is hardcoded `readonly approval = "write" as const;` at mcp/tool-bridge.ts:656 and `DeferredMCPTool.approval` is the identical hardcode at tool-bridge.ts:771 — both unconditional, neither derived from the server's config, so a stdio server that spawns a subprocess and an http server that POSTs to a remote host sit in the same tier. Meanwhile the extension tool path defaults STRICTER: `ToolDefinition.approval` (extensions/types.ts:658) is documented as defaulting to `"exec"` when omitted. So the naive reading of 'parity' is backwards — an extension-registered tool is already gated at `exec` while an MCP tool is gated at `write`. Corollary the design must address: the branch at tools/approval.ts:369-371, `if (tool.name.startsWith("mcp__") && tool.approval === undefined) { lines.push("Origin: MCP server tool"); }`, is currently UNREACHABLE for manager-minted MCP tools, because both classes always set `approval` — so the approval prompt never tells the user the call came from an MCP server. If a contributed server lands in that same path, the user gets a `write`-tier prompt with no origin line, which is exactly the disclosure gap a trust decision is supposed to close. The design must state whether contributed servers get a distinct tier and whether the origin line becomes reachable.

plan_corrections.claim: Plan §WI-12: contributing a server 'inherits WI-0's unanswered posture'.
plan_corrections.verdict: UNDERSTATED — it is not just unanswered, it is hardcoded permissive, which is stronger evidence than the plan gives
plan_corrections.correction: `isProjectTrusted(): boolean` is declared twice on the extension-facing surfaces (extensions/types.ts:494 and :561) and implemented as `isProjectTrusted: () => true` at extensions/runner.ts:1264 and again at session/agent-session.ts:7406. There is no gate to inherit — the value is a constant. So a design that says 'extension-contributed servers land in the same tier as project `.mcp.json` servers' is, as of this HEAD, saying 'no tier at all'. State that in the document explicitly; it converts an abstract dependency on WI-0 into a checkable precondition (`grep -n 'isProjectTrusted: () => true'` must stop returning two hits before the trust tier in this design means anything).
plan_corrections.evidence: `grep -rn 'isProjectTrusted' packages/coding-agent/src` → 4 hits: extensions/types.ts:494, extensions/types.ts:561, extensions/runner.ts:1264, session/agent-session.ts:7406.

open_questions: TRUST TIER — the one that must be answered in the document, not deferred: an MCP server contributed by a loaded extension lands in which tier, and who authorizes the connection? Concretely, is it (a) same tier as a project `.mcp.json` server, i.e. auto-connect on load, (b) same tier as a user-scope server but gated on the extension being trusted, so it inherits WI-0's answer, or (c) always require an explicit per-server user grant before the first connect. This is not a detail: (a) means any loaded extension can open an outbound network connection to an arbitrary URL with no prompt, which is a materially larger blast radius than registering a tool. If the document picks (a) without saying so in those words, it has not answered the question. Note the current stub makes all three look identical in code today — see the isProjectTrusted correction — so the choice is invisible until someone changes the stub.

Does the descriptor have to be declared at load time only, or can a live extension register a server later (from a tool call, an event handler)? The plan does not say. Declarative-only (load-time) is strictly smaller and is what the existing package path does; imperative-late is what 'extension' usually implies and it is the case that forces a runtime `connectServers` call on a hot path. Recommend load-time-only in the document and say why — a late register is a new event on the manager, and that is WI-7's registerMode problem wearing a different hat.

Credential ownership: a contributed server with `auth.type === "oauth"` needs a credential slot. The core OAuth store is keyed by server URL (`mcpOAuthCredentialIdsForServerUrl`, mcp/oauth-credentials.ts:24) and the refresh path writes back through `refreshManagedMcpOAuthCredential` (:105) / `refreshStoredManagedMcpOAuthCredential` (:159). If an extension may contribute an OAuth server, an extension-authored `url` can collide with a user's existing credential id for that URL. The document must say whether contributed servers are ineligible for managed OAuth, or whether credential resolution is namespaced per extension. Leaving this unstated is how a third-party extension ends up reading a user's token for a URL it chose.

Enable/disable semantics: today the dashboard toggle for a non-native, non-mcp-json source deliberately does NOT write the source file — `#writableMcpSourcePath` (packages/tui/src/overlays/extensions/extension-dashboard.ts:449-453) allowlists exactly `native` and `mcp-json` and returns `undefined` otherwise, so the toggle falls through to the user-level `disabledServers` / `enabledServers` denylist/allowlist in `setMcpServerEnabled` (mcp/config-writer.ts:333-380, the trailing else-branch). A descriptor-contributed server lands in that same bucket. Confirm that is the intended UX (a per-user off switch that survives the extension being present) rather than an extension-owned `enabled` flag that the user's toggle must not be able to override.

Does this design decide the write surface, or does it defer to WI-10? The plan lists WI-10 as a dependency, and this document should state the MCP answer as a PROPOSAL to be reconciled with WI-10 rather than as a settled canonical-surface claim. If WI-10 has already landed by the time this is written, this is a one-line reconciliation instead — check before writing.

steps.instruction: Confirm the tree before trusting any line number in this spec: `git -C /Users/tranquangdang21/Projects/ultraworkers rev-parse --short HEAD` returns `808b365`. STOP GATE — do not write a single line of the design document until the trust tier (open question 1) has an answer from a human, in writing. Recommended: option (b), same tier as a user-scope server, gated on the extension being trusted — which means the design is explicitly BLOCKED on WI-0, and says so. Option (a) (auto-connect, no gate) is only defensible if WI-0 chose a per-directory trust prompt, because otherwise it is an unconditional outbound-connection primitive. Option (c) (explicit per-server grant) is the safe default and costs the most friction. Whichever is chosen, it must be one sentence a reviewer can disagree with, not a paragraph that hedges. This is the failure mode the plan names: a design written as though the approval question were settled, so the implementation picks silently.

Re-read the five verified MCP-extension members so the document describes the CURRENT state accurately and does not inherit the plan's overstatement: `sed -n '655,676p;898,918p;1256,1257p;1338,1342p' packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/types.ts`. Establish the correction the plan most needs, because it changes the recommendation: an extension PACKAGE already contributes MCP servers declaratively. Read `sed -n '275,280p;293,300p;355,370p;423,429p' packages/coding-agent/src/discovery/omp-plugins.ts` and confirm the two sibling providers at `discovery/agent-plugins.ts:335` and `discovery/claude-plugins.ts:737`. The design document must open by stating the gap correctly: declarative package contribution SHIPS, imperative runtime contribution does not exist. Do not write 'extensions cannot contribute MCP servers' anywhere in the document — it is false and a reviewer who knows the codebase will stop reading.

Write the two architectures as genuine alternatives, each with its failure mode. (A) SERVER DESCRIPTOR: the extension hands core a descriptor; core stamps `_source`, owns credentials and the connection lifecycle, and calls the already-public `MCPManager.connectServers`; teardown is `disconnectServer(name)` keyed by `mcpServerName`. (B) CONFIG WRITE: the extension writes MCP config itself. For (B) write down the concrete damage, not the slogan: it creates a second store outside the capability registry (the problem WI-8a Option A exists to solve), it puts extension-authored data into a file that `setMcpServerEnabled` will later rewrite, and it reproduces verbatim a failure mode the dashboard already works around for package-contributed servers — `#writableMcpSourcePath` at packages/tui/src/overlays/extensions/extension-dashboard.ts:449-453 allowlists only `native` and `mcp-json`, so a plugin-owned file is never written. Cite that function by name; it is the strongest argument in the document and it is already in the tree.

Record the recommendation (A) with the reason, and — the load-bearing finding — state that it requires NO new lifecycle. Read `sed -n '656,700p' packages/coding-agent/src/mcp/manager.ts` and write down four facts: `connectServers` is public and already incremental; it accepts a `Record<string, SourceMeta>` and stamps it onto both `#sources` and any existing connection's `_source` (:690-696); it skips names already connected or in flight (:700-712); and `disconnectServer(name)` is the symmetric teardown (:1242). Then read the ownership comment at :937-941 and adopt its rule explicitly: ownership is matched via `mcpServerName`, never a sanitized `mcp__<name>_` name prefix, because 'atlassian' can prefix 'atlassian:atlassian' and a server with sanitized characters never prefix-matches its own tools. This is the single most useful thing the document delivers — it turns 'large M-sized build' into 'a producer for two records plus an owner index'.

Type the proposed descriptor against the canonical shape and say what it drops. `sed -n '15,74p' packages/coding-agent/src/capability/mcp.ts` — the descriptor is `MCPServer` MINUS `_source` (core owns provenance; an extension must never be able to forge where a server came from). Call out the three hardening axes by name and say whether a contributed server inherits them: `envPolicy: "literal"` (:36), `envLiteralKeys` (:38), `headerPolicy: "origin-locked"` (:50). An extension-contributed server that silently opts out of origin-locked header pinning forwards configured headers across origins. If the document does not resolve these, the build will.

Write the approval-parity proposition with the real numbers, and flag the finding the plan could not have had. The tiers today are: `MCPTool.approval` hardcoded `readonly approval = "write" as const;` at mcp/tool-bridge.ts:656; `DeferredMCPTool.approval` the identical hardcode at :771 — both unconditional, neither derived from the server's config, so a stdio server spawning a subprocess and an http server POSTing to a remote host share one tier. Extension-registered tools default STRICTER: `ToolDefinition.approval` at extensions/types.ts:658 is documented to default to `"exec"` when omitted. So the naive reading of 'parity' is backwards and the document must say so. Then record the reachable-branch finding: tools/approval.ts:369-371 pushes 'Origin: MCP server tool' only when `tool.name.startsWith("mcp__") && tool.approval === undefined`, and since both MCP tool classes always set `approval`, that line can never fire for a manager-minted tool — so today the approval prompt never discloses MCP origin. Decide explicitly whether contributed servers get a distinct tier and whether that line becomes reachable; silence here is what the plan warns about.

State the WI-0 dependency as a checkable precondition rather than a vibe. Write: `isProjectTrusted(): boolean` is declared at extensions/types.ts:494 and :561 and hardcoded `() => true` at extensions/runner.ts:1264 and session/agent-session.ts:7406, so today the trust check cannot fail. Therefore 'contributed servers inherit the project trust tier' is, at this HEAD, equivalent to 'contributed servers have no tier' — and the precondition for this design meaning anything is that `grep -n 'isProjectTrusted: () => true' packages/coding-agent/src` stops returning two hits. A design that names a tier without this sentence is describing a tier that does not exist.

Answer the credential question (open question 3) or mark it explicitly unresolved with an owner. The core OAuth store is keyed by server URL — `mcpOAuthCredentialIdsForServerUrl` at mcp/oauth-credentials.ts:24 — and refresh writes back through `refreshManagedMcpOAuthCredential` (:105). An extension that may contribute an OAuth server can therefore name a URL for which the user already holds a credential. The document must either make contributed servers ineligible for managed OAuth or state that credential resolution is namespaced per extension. Do not leave this as prose that sounds decided.

Answer the enable/disable question (open question 4) using the code, not intuition. Trace `setMcpServerEnabled` (mcp/config-writer.ts:333-380): when the server is not found in any writable candidate path, disabling adds it to the user-level `disabledServers` denylist and enabling adds it to the `enabledServers` allowlist. State which bucket a descriptor-contributed server lands in, and confirm the intended UX is a per-user off switch that survives the extension being installed — not an extension-owned `enabled` flag the user's toggle cannot override.

Write the 'not decided here' section, and put the build's non-ownership in it. §8.2 of the plan records that MCP contribution has no owner and no milestone, and the plan has no concept of phases — so the document must not say 'Phase 4' or 'Phase 5'. State instead: this design is merged under M2; the build is unowned; a name and a deadline must be assigned before M2 closes. Recommend the build be scheduled AFTER WI-9 (wave 7), since unloading an extension that owns a live connection is a resource-inventory problem WI-9 solves, not a new one.

Add the two pointer lines: one in docs/extensions.md near :392 recording that a loaded extension cannot currently contribute an MCP server and pointing at the new doc; one in docs/mcp-config.md at :40 or in the precedence list at :484-495 recording that package-level declarative contribution DOES ship while imperative runtime contribution is designed-not-built. Both are one line. Do not expand either section.

gate_can_fail:
Yes, on four of the five clauses, and it is worth being precise about which. Clause (b) fails hard and mechanically: touch any file under packages/ and `git diff --stat HEAD` shows it. Clause (c) fails if the document repeats the plan's overstatement — that is a real check because the plan's own text contains the error and an engineer following it faithfully will reproduce it. Clause (d) fails only if a human is disciplined; nothing mechanical detects an unanswered trust tier, which is exactly why it is written as a hard clause rather than a suggestion. Clause (e) fails only on a human read.

What the gate CANNOT catch, and the spec should not pretend otherwise: it cannot detect a design that names a trust tier and is wrong about it, and it cannot detect the design being quietly turned into a build plan by a later reader who skims the 'not decided here' section. That is the human dependency §11.3's assignment requirement exists for. The one mechanical counterweight is clause (b), which catches the most common failure — someone 'just adding the method' because the design made it look easy.
